[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) Architecture & Mechanics"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) represent the foundational architecture for modern computer vision tasks. Unlike standard Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs), CNNs are specifically designed to process grid-like data, such as images, by exploiting spatial local correlations."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Components of CNN Architecture"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Convolutional Layers: Extract local features like edges, corners, and textures using learnable filters."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pooling Layers: Downsample feature maps to reduce spatial dimensions, computational complexity, and parameters."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Activation Functions: Introduce non-linearity into the network, typically using ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit)."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fully Connected Layers: Flatten the high-level semantic feature maps to perform the final classification or regression."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing a Basic CNN in PyTorch"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class SimpleCNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(SimpleCNN, self).__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=3, out_channels=16, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(16 * 16 * 16, 10)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv1(x)
        x = self.relu(x)
        x = self.pool(x)
        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)
        x = self.fc(x)
        return x"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Mechanics of the Convolution Operation"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"The convolution operation involves sliding a small kernel over the input matrix, computing element-wise multiplication, and summing the results into a single output pixel in the feature map. Parameters like stride and padding dictate how the spatial dimensions evolve through layers."}]
